name: React
one_liner: Component-based UI library, and the default assumption of most frontend job descriptions.
what_it_is: A library for building user interfaces from composable components, with state changes driving re-renders through a virtual DOM diff. Modern React centres on hooks and, increasingly, on server components that render on the server and stream to the client.
why_it_matters: React is less a choice than a baseline: it shapes hiring, tutorials and the surrounding tool ecosystem, so understanding it is close to mandatory even if you never pick it. The genuinely current shift is server components, which move a meaningful share of work back to the server and invalidate a lot of client-side patterns people learned between 2018 and 2022.
suitable_for: Applications where you need the largest available hiring pool and ecosystem
Products with complex, highly interactive client state
not_suitable_for: Content-heavy sites that ship far more JavaScript than they need
Small teams wanting a framework that makes decisions for them — React deliberately does not
Projects that cannot absorb the churn of its evolving server-rendering story
